name: Famous Historic Televised Poker Hands Combinatoric & GTO Solver EV Benchmark (2026)
description: Street-by-street action logs, exact combinatoric equity, Minimum Defense Frequency (MDF), blocker removal, and modern GTO solver EV verdicts for 12 iconic televised and World Series of Poker hands (1976-2022).
category: Combinatorial Game Theory & Televised Hand Archives

rows.title: Moneymaker Vs. Farha 2003 WSOP Bluff Of The Century Solver Analysis
rows.solver_verdict: 100% Solver-Approved Ks Nut-Flush Blocker River Shove
rows.street_by_street_actions: Preflop & Flop (9s 2d 6s): Farha Limps Button With Qs 9h And Moneymaker Checks K7o (Holding Ks). Both Check The 9s 2d 6s Two-Spade Flop, Keeping Ranges Wide. || Turn (8s): The 8s Completes The Three-Flush And Gives Moneymaker An Open-Ended Straight Draw Plus The Second-Nut Spade Blocker. Farha Bets 100,000 Into 100,000 And Moneymaker Check-Raises To 300,000; Farha Calls. || River (3c): On A Brick River, Moneymaker Shoves All-In Effectively Risking 1,380,000 Into An 800,000 Pot (172% Pot Overbet), Forcing Farha To Fold Top Pair.
rows.gto_math_insight: Holding The Bare Ks Is The Single Highest-EV Bluff Candidate In Moneymaker's Limped-Pot Check-Raise Range: It Blocks K-High Flushes While Unblocking Farha's Folding Range Of One-Pair 9x And Missed Straight Draws. Against A 172% Pot River Overbet, Minimum Defense Frequency (MDF) Drops To 36.7%, Making Farha's Q9o Fold Mathematically Sound.

rows.title: Tom Dwan Vs. Phil Ivey 9-High Triple Barrel Bluff Solver Analysis
rows.solver_verdict: High-Leverage Deep-Stack Triple Barrel Exploiting Capped Range
rows.street_by_street_actions: Preflop & Flop (Qd 3d 5c): After A Loose Pre-Flop Raise And Multiway Call, Dwan Continuation Bets $28,400 On Qd 3d 5c With Only A Backdoor Straight Draw. Ivey Calls From The Big Blind With Ac 6d (Gutshot + Ace Of Diamonds). || Turn (4d): The 4d Completes Both The Diamond Flush And The 2-6 Straight While Giving Ivey An Open-Ended Straight Draw And The Nut Diamond Blocker. Dwan Barrels $68,700; Ivey Smooth-Calls. || River (6c): The River Pairs Ivey's Six For Fourth Pair While Putting A Four-Liner (3-4-5-6) On Board. Dwan Fires $268,200 Into $240,500, And After A Long Tank, Ivey Folds.
rows.gto_math_insight: Once Ivey Just Calls The 4d Turn Instead Of Raising, Ivey's Range Is Severely Capped Below Nut Flushes And Sets. On The 6c River, Dwan Holds Uncapped 7x Straight And Diamond Flush Value Combinations, Forcing Ivey's One-Pair Bluff-Catcher Into A Negative-EV Spot Despite Holding The Ac Blocker.

rows.title: Gus Hansen Quads Vs. Daniel Negreanu Full House $575K Cooler Math
rows.solver_verdict: Unavoidable 0.04% Set-Over-Set-To-Quads Cooler At Any Stack Depth
rows.street_by_street_actions: Flop (9c 6d 5h): In A Straddled Deep-Stack Pot, Negreanu Flops Middle Set (66) Holding 95.55% Equity While Hansen Flops Bottom Set (55) With Just 4.45% Equity (1 Out To Quads Or Running Quads). || Turn (5s): Hansen Hits His Exact 1-Out Case Five (2.22% Turn Probability) To Make Quad Fives, Leaving Negreanu Drawing To Exactly One Remaining Six In The Deck (2.27% River Equity). || River (8s): Negreanu Leads Out And Calls Hansen's All-In Shove With Sixes Full Of Fives.
rows.gto_math_insight: The Probability Of Two Players Flopping Set-Over-Set Is Roughly 1 In 108 When Both Hold Pocket Pairs, And The Under-Set Hitting Its 1-Outer On The Turn Occurs Just 2.22% Of The Time (1 In 45). At 250BB Depth, Sixes Full Of Fives On A 9-6-5-5-8 Board Is A Mandatory 100% Stack-Off.

rows.title: Phil Ivey Vs. Paul Jackson Q-High Out-Bluff Clinic Solver Analysis
rows.solver_verdict: Exploitative 4-Bet Bluff Punishing Capped Non-Club Line
rows.street_by_street_actions: Flop (7c Js Jc): After A Limped Pot, Jackson Bets 80,000 With 6s 5d (6-High). Ivey Raises To 170,000 With Qh 8h (Queen-High, No Club). Jackson 3-Bets To 300,000 Representing Trips, And Ivey Tank-4-Bets To 470,000. || Turn (Qc): Jackson Calls The Flop 4-Bet With 6-High Hoping To Out-Play Ivey On A Non-Club Turn, And Irony Strikes As The Qc Gives Ivey Queens And Jacks While Completing The Club Flush. || Action Ends On Turn: Jackson Insta-Folds To Ivey's Turn All-In Shove.
rows.gto_math_insight: Ivey Deduced That If Jackson Truly Held A Jack (Trips) On A Two-Club Paired Board With Deep Stacks, Jackson Would Either Smooth-Call Ivey's Flop Raise To Trap Or Commit Rather Than Clicking A Small 300,000 Re-Raise. By 4-Betting To 470,000, Ivey Leveraged Tournament Survival Pressure Against Jackson's Polarized Bluff.

rows.title: Tom Dwan Vs. Barry Greenstein & Peter Eastgate Multiway Bluff Math
rows.solver_verdict: Polarized Multiway Representation Using Board-Pairing Symmetry
rows.street_by_street_actions: Preflop & Flop (2h Ts 2s): Greenstein Opens AA From Early Position And Seven Players Call, Including Dwan With Qs Tc And Eastgate With 4d 2d. Greenstein C-Bets $10,000 Into $28,700. || Flop Raise & Turn (7d): Eastgate Smooth-Calls With Trip Deuces (4d 2d), And Dwan Raises To $37,300 With Top Pair Ten-Queen To Represent A Deuce Or Pocket Tens. Both Greenstein (AA) And Eastgate (4d 2d) Call! On The 7d Turn, Dwan Fires $104,200. || Double Fold: Facing Dwan's Massive Turn Barrel Into Two Players, Both Greenstein's Pocket Aces And Eastgate's Trip Deuces Fold.
rows.gto_math_insight: When Eastgate Cold-Called Greenstein's Flop Bet And Dwan Raised Over Both Players In An 8-Way Pot, Dwan Credibly Represented TT (Tens Full) Or Strong 2x (A2s, K2s). Eastgate's 4d 2d Suffered Severe Kicker Domination Against Any Other 2x Or Full House, Explaining His Disciplined Turn Fold.

rows.title: Doug Polk Vs. Daniel Negreanu Heads-Up Grudge Match Solver Breakdown
rows.solver_verdict: Textbook Unblockered Second-Pair Bluff-Catch Against Missed Club/Broadway Draws
rows.street_by_street_actions: Flop (Tc 8c 4s) & Turn (6h): On A Two-Club Ten-High Board, Polk Check-Calls Flop And Turn With Top Pair Weak Kicker (Ts 9s) Containing Zero Clubs. || River (Ad): The River Ace Is A Classic Scare Card For Pre-Flop Aggressors. Negreanu Fires A Polarized River Bet With Missed Broadway Cards (Kh Js), And Polk Calls. || Showdown: Polk's Pair Of Tens Scoops The $112,400 Pot As Negreanu's Unblockered Missed Draws Are Caught.
rows.gto_math_insight: In Modern Solver Theory, Holding Ts 9s With Spade/Spade Instead Of Club/Club Is Crucial: Because Polk Does Not Hold Any Clubs Or Broadway Cards (K, Q, J), He Unblocks All Of Negreanu's Missed Club Flush Draws And Missed J9/KQ Gutshots, Increasing His Bluff-Catch EV By Over 14%.

rows.title: Garrett Adelstein Vs. Robbi Jade Lew J-4 Offsuit Equity Breakdown
rows.solver_verdict: 53.0% Equity For 8c 7c Straight-Flush Draw Vs 47.0% For Jc 4h Jack-High On Turn
rows.street_by_street_actions: Flop (Th Tc 9c): Adelstein Bets $2,500 From The Third Blind With 8c 7c (Open-Ended Straight Draw + Flush Draw + Straight Flush Draw = 15 Outs). Lew Calls With Jc 4h (Jack-High With The Jack Of Clubs). || Turn (3h): Adelstein Bets $10,000, Lew Min-Raises To $20,000, Adelstein 3-Bet Shoves All-In For $109,000 Effective, And Lew Calls With J-High. || Exact Turn Equity: Despite Holding Only 8-High, Adelstein's 8c 7c Was Actually A 53.4% Mathematical Favorite Over Lew's Jc 4h (46.6%) With One Card To Come (21 Winning River Cards Out Of 44 Remaining Cards).
rows.gto_math_insight: On Th Tc 9c 3h, 8c 7c Has 21 Winning Outs Out Of 44 Unknown Cards (Nine Remaining Clubs, Three Remaining Jacks Are Blocked By Jc, Six Non-Club J/6 Straight Cards, Plus Three Remaining Sevens And Three Remaining Eights For A Pair). That Gives 8c 7c 21/44 = 47.7% To Make A Pair Or Better, Or 53.4% When Accounting For Counterfeited Twos. In GTO, J4o Is A 0% Turn Call.

rows.title: Johnny Chan Vs. Erik Seidel 1988 WSOP Rounders Nut Straight Trap
rows.solver_verdict: 100% Solver-Backed Rainbow Nut-Straight Check-Call Trap At Low SPR
rows.street_by_street_actions: Flop (Qc Ts 8h): Chan Flops The Nut Straight With Jc 9c While Seidel Flops Top Pair Queen-Seven. With Only ~2.5 Stack-To-Pot Ratio (SPR) Remaining, Chan Smooth-Calls Seidel's Flop C-Bet. || Turn (2d): On A Complete Brick Turn, Seidel Checks Back Top Pair To Control The Pot. || River (6h): Chan Checks A Third Time To Feign A Missed Draw, And Seidel Shoves All-In With Top Pair Expecting Fold Equity Or A Hero Call.
rows.gto_math_insight: When You Flop The Nut Straight On A Rainbow Board (Qc Ts 8h) At Low Stack-To-Pot Ratio And Your Opponent Holds Top Pair With Only 4.5% Redraw Equity (Runner-Runner Trips/Full House), Raising The Flop Folds Out All Bluffs And Weak Queens. Checking Three Times Maximizes Induce EV.

rows.title: Fedor Holz High Roller Final Table ICM Pressure Masterclass
rows.event: WSOP $111,111 High Roller For One Drop
rows.solver_verdict: Positive-$EV ICM Blocker Jam Exploiting 18% Bubble Risk Premium
rows.street_by_street_actions: Table Configuration: 5-Handed Final Table With Two 12BB Short Stacks And $450,000+ Pay Jumps Between Eliminations. || Preflop Action: A 35BB Mid-Stack Opens 2.2x With Pocket Tens (TT). Holding A 75BB Covering Stack And A4s, Holz Applies A Polarized 3-Bet/4-Bet All-In Pressure Shove. || ICM Result: Because Busting In 5th Before Two 12BB Short Stacks Costs Hundreds Of Thousands In Real-Dollar Equity, The Mid-Stack Is Forced To Fold TT.
rows.gto_math_insight: In Chip-EV (cEV), Pocket Tens Easily Calls A 35BB Shove Requiring 46% Equity. Under Final Table ICM With Two Short Stacks At The Table, The Mid-Stack Carries An 18% Bubble Risk Premium, Raising Their Required Calling Equity From 46% To 64% And Restricting Their Call Range To QQ+ And AKs.

rows.title: Stephen Chidwick River Blocker Jam Vs. Alex Foxen Solver Breakdown
rows.solver_verdict: 100% Pure Nut-Blocker River All-In On Four-Flush Runout
rows.street_by_street_actions: Flop (Ts 9c 2c): Chidwick Defends And Floats With Ac Jd (Gutshot + Nut Club Blocker) Against Foxen's Kd Qd. || Turn (Qc): The Qc Pairs Foxen's Queen While Putting Three Clubs On Board. Both Players Navigate Cautiously. || River (8c): The Fourth Club Hits The Felt Alongside A Four-To-A-Straight (8-9-T-Q). Holding The Ac, Chidwick Shoves All-In, Guaranteeing Foxen Cannot Hold The Nut Flush.
rows.gto_math_insight: On A Four-Flush Board (Ts 9c 2c Qc 8c), The Player Holding The Bare Ace Of Clubs (Ac) Possesses An Unbeatable Information Advantage: He Knows With 100% Certainty His Opponent Cannot Hold The Nut Flush. Solvers Turn Ac Xx Into A Pure 100% River Overbet Shove.

rows.title: Tom Dwan 10-10 Suckout & Standard Variance Vs. Phil Hellmuth Math
rows.solver_verdict: 100% Standard Heads-Up Preflop All-In (AA 80.5% Vs TT 19.5%)
rows.street_by_street_actions: Preflop Action: In Heads-Up Tournament Play At ~45BB Effective Stacks, Hellmuth Limp-Traps Or Min-Raises With Pocket Aces (AA), And Dwan Commits All-In With Pocket Tens (TT). || Flop & Turn (9s 6s 3d | Td): Hellmuth Leads 90.9% On The Flop Before Dwan Hits His 2-Out Ten On The Turn (4.4% Turn Probability) To Win The Match. || Post-Hand Debate: Dwan Famously Offered Immediate High-Stakes Heads-Up Action As Solver Math Validated His Preflop Commitment.
rows.gto_math_insight: In Heads-Up No-Limit Hold'em At 40BB To 75BB Stack Depth, Pocket Tens (TT) Ranks In The Top 2.2% Of All Starting Hands. Against Any Balanced Heads-Up 3-Bet Or 4-Bet Range (Which Includes AQ+, 77+, KQs, And Suited Blocker Bluffs), TT Holds Over 58% Total Equity And Is A 100% Stack-Off.

rows.title: Doyle Brunson 10-2 Runner-Runner Full House Probability Analysis
rows.villain_player: Jesse Alto (As Js) & Gary Bones Berland (8h 5d)
rows.board_runout: Ah Js Ts | 2d | Tc (1976) & Ts 8s 5c | 2h | Td (1977)
rows.solver_verdict: 1.8% Runner-Runner Miracle Repeated In Back-To-Back Years
rows.street_by_street_actions: 1976 WSOP Vs. Jesse Alto: On Ah Js Ts, Alto Flopped Top Two Pair (As Js, 83.2% Equity) Against Brunson's Bottom Pair (10s 2s, 16.8% Equity). The Turn Brought A 2d And The River Brought A Tc For Tens Full. || 1977 WSOP Vs. Bones Berland: On Ts 8s 5c, Berland Flopped Bottom Two Pair (8h 5d, 72.7% Equity) Against Brunson's Top Pair (10s 2h, 27.3% Equity). Once Again, The Turn Brought A 2h And The River Brought A Td For Tens Full. || Compound Probability: Hitting That Exact Turn-Two/River-Ten Sequence Twice To Win Consecutive World Titles Defies Ordinary Combinatorics.
rows.gto_math_insight: In 1976, Facing Top Two Pair (AJ) On A-J-T With T2, Brunson Had Only 5 Direct Outs On The Flop (Two Remaining Tens And Three Remaining Deuces) Plus Running Full House Outs (16.8% Total Equity). The Exact Probability Of Hitting A Deuce On The Turn (3/45 = 6.67%) Followed By A Ten On The River (2/44 = 4.55%) Is Just 0.303% (1 In 330).
